structural_memory.memory: Vessel design is a multi-role engineering chain rather than a single shipyard output. Structurally distinct roles include owner/newbuilding requirements, yard design office, independent naval architect or specialist consultant, classification plan-approval function, model-test or analysis capability, equipment OEM/system integrator and the eventual operator.

A design-basis or owner-requirement state precedes detailed engineering. Mission, cargo/trade assumptions, capacity, speed/efficiency targets, regulatory/class constraints and maintainability expectations can change over time, so the design basis needs versioned known-time rather than a timeless specification.

General arrangement and principal geometry act as coordination states across cargo capacity, machinery spaces, access, accommodation and safety systems. Exact dimensions are vessel-specific Evidence, but design maturity and interface dependence are reusable structural memory.

Hull-form, hydrostatics and powering/performance prediction form an analysis layer separate from actual sea performance. Predicted resistance, propulsion or efficiency outcomes should not be treated as realized operating facts.

Stability is a design-and-verification state with assumptions, loading conditions and later as-built inputs. A design calculation or approval is not interchangeable with the vessel's later physical loading/condition state or an operational stability judgment.

Structural design is a distinct engineering layer involving load assumptions, material/arrangement decisions and approval/revision states. Exact scantlings, loads and rules remain Evidence, while structural maturity and late-change propagation are useful Memory categories.

Machinery arrangement and maintainability are design states, not only equipment-selection facts. Space, access, redundancy, piping/cabling interfaces, removal routes and serviceability can create later maintenance or repair constraints even when individual machinery items are technically adequate.

Systems integration is its own maturity state. Electrical, automation/control, piping, communications, safety and cargo systems can each be locally complete while cross-system interfaces, signals, power dependencies or control logic remain unresolved.

Model testing, simulation or specialist analysis are prediction/validation inputs with scope and known-time, not final truth. The relationship between design model, assumptions, measured model-test result and later full-scale performance must remain explicit.

Plan submission, review, comments, approval and resubmission form a separate assurance workflow. Approval status can constrain construction or change release, but approval itself does not prove the as-built vessel, later condition or legal seaworthiness.

Design change is a lifecycle state with ripple effects. A late owner, yard, class or supplier change can propagate through weight, space, interfaces, procurement, construction sequence, testing and schedule rather than remaining a local drawing revision.

Weight growth and center-of-gravity/configuration change are useful design-control states because accumulated local modifications can affect performance, stability margin and payload assumptions even before an obvious operational defect exists. Exact values remain vessel-specific Evidence.

As-built configuration and technical handover are separate from design-intent completion. Drawings, equipment lists, settings, manuals and change records can lag or diverge from installed reality, influencing maintenance, retrofit and later investigation.

Classification plan approval should remain separate from physical condition, construction quality and actual performance; it is an assurance state over submitted design information, not self-executing proof of the finished vessel.

Repair, conversion and retrofit work inherit the original design basis and interface constraints. A retrofit is therefore not merely an equipment swap; it may reopen weight, structural, power, space, stability or systems-integration dependencies.

Equipment-OEM changes can propagate beyond procurement into foundation/interface design, controls, power, cooling, piping, testing and documentation; supplier substitution and design maturity should therefore be separately clocked.

Casualty or performance analysis should distinguish original design intent, approved design revision, as-built configuration, later modification and event-time physical/operational state rather than attributing a later outcome directly to the nominal design.
Shipyard project, repair/conversion and classification-survey roles overlap earlier Shipping memory, though P066 adds the upstream design-engineering state machine.
Plan approval and design-document follow-up partially overlap the classification/statutory assurance layer recovered in P063.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: Exact hull dimensions, hydrostatics, stability criteria, structural scantlings, power predictions and model-test values are too vessel- and calculation-specific for blind retention.
Exact class rules, plan-approval requirements, regulatory design criteria and approval chronology require dated authoritative Evidence.
Named naval-architecture firms, model basins, shipyard design offices, consultants, OEMs and system integrators are not retained as a provider directory.
Exact design defects, performance shortfalls, change orders and named-vessel as-built divergences require claim-scoped Evidence.
negative_space: Exact design calculations, rule checks and vessel-specific engineering margins.
Private/regional naval-architecture, engineering-consulting, model-test and systems-integration provider lineages.
Historical non-English predecessor terminology for naval architecture, plan approval and ship-design engineering.
Named-vessel design evolution, approved revisions, as-built configuration and current technical status.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only orientation/source-discovery output. It is not naval-architecture, stability, structural, engineering, classification, safety, performance or regulatory advice and does not establish any named vessel, design, yard, consultant, model-test, approval or performance fact.
stop_reason: The upstream vessel-design engineering lifecycle is recalled at useful structural resolution. Further depth would become calculation-, rule-, vessel-, yard-, consultant-, supplier- or jurisdiction-specific and should be deferred to Evidence rather than blind engineering detail.
